channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

Nature Communications: Cell-inspired dual-tandem catalytic nanoreactors drive targeted hearing protection
item.description: Here, the authors present a biomimetic nanoreactor that mimics natural antioxidant enzymes, rebuilds cochlear redox homeostasis and protects against noise‑induced hearing loss by preserving hair cells and synaptic function.

item.title: Nature Communications: A programmable lipid-triggered allosteric site modulates LC3 LIR receptor binding activity
item.description: The allosteric mechanisms by which lipid binding controls protein activity remain poorly understood. Here, the authors identify a lipid-triggered allosteric site in LC3 that remodels its receptor-binding interface upon membrane interaction. This site can be engineered to precisely tune LC3-LIR interactions, offering a new strategy to regulate selective autophagy.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD97/ ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma
item.description: Allergic asthma involves different lung cells and mediators. Here, the authors examine the function of CD97/ ADGRE5 and show that its absence increases the severity of allergic lung inflammation in mice. Allergen-pulsed Cd97 -/- DCs are more activated and promote stronger type 2 immune responses than WT DCs and, in humans, lung DCs from allergen-exposed asthmatics express less CD97 than allergic non-asthmatics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Wireless IoT-enabled microneedle electroceutical for personalized and connected pain management
item.description: Skin-attached electrotherapeutic devices suffer from unstable skin-electrode interface. Here, the authors present a thermoresponsive conductive adhesive microneedle electroceutical providing stable, safe stimulation and IoT-based personalized pain therapy with healthcare-provider oversight.

item.title: Nature Communications: Why variant effect predictors and multiplexed assays agree and disagree
item.description: Multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) and computational variant effect predictors (VEPs) are two key tools for the interpretation of genetic variants. Here the authors compare the results from these two approaches and investigate instances where they produce conflicting evidence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Towards density-optimal DNA storage with practical bijective coding
item.description: Existing DNA storage methods struggle to avoid error-prone sequences while retaining usable ones. Here the authors develop Siyuan Code, a bijective codec that avoids high-error patterns, utilises all suitable strands, and reaches 1.66 bits/nucleotide, 41 EB/gram, and only uses 6 copies/strand.

item.title: Nature Communications: The endo-lysosomal system drives lumen formation in a human epiblast model
item.description: Rengarajan et al. identify RAB35- and RAB7-regulated endo-lysosomal dynamics as important drivers of the formation of the apicosome and lumen formation in a model of human epiblast formation. This study presents new insights into peri-implantation human embryo morphogenesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Whole-brain, all-optical interrogation of neuronal dynamics underlying gut and vascular interoception in zebrafish
item.description: Understanding how the brain processes signals from other organs has been limited by a lack of tools. Here the authors introduce an all-optical system for gut or vascular nutrient release during whole-brain imaging in zebrafish.

item.title: Nature Communications: An AI-powered self-driving microscope for low-cost acute leukemia detection
item.description: Current AI systems for leukemia detection typically rely on costly whole-slide scanners, limiting accessibility in low-resource settings. Here, the authors present ALLocate, a low-cost, AI-driven microscope plugin that enables self-driving microscopy for accurate and affordable leukemia detection without whole-slide scanners.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bacterial ribonucleoprotein bodies maintain an acidic pH environment as a mechanism of enzyme regulation
item.description: Ratiometric pH sensors show that phase-separated BR-bodies in Caulobacter crescentus form acidic interiors, tuned by scaffold protein charge, to regulate enzymatic activity. Disrupting this pH control impairs stationary phase recovery and causes stress-induced morphological defects.

item.title: Nature Communications: Psilocybin enhances sociability only in altered behavioural state and does not need an awake experience to be effective
item.description: Psilocybin shows therapeutic effects in the treatment of neuropsychiatric conditions but it can also cause strong hallucinations. Here, the authors show that psilocybin can improve social symptoms in a mouse model of autism, an effect that does not depend on wakefulness during the acute drug effects, suggesting that it might be possible to develop treatments that keep the benefits while avoiding the mind-altering side effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: ALKBH5-mediated microglia-neuron crosstalk inhibits sympathetic innervation and adipocyte browning in male mice
item.description: Interactions between nervous system and adipose tissue are involved in the regulation of adipocyte browning, but the role of microglia is incompletely understood. In this study, the authors demonstrate that RNA m6A demethylase ALKBH5 in the microglia of the nucleus of hypothalamus (PVH) region inhibit cold exposure-induced adipocyte browning in the subcutaneous white adipose tissue of male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: dioscRi enables transferable prediction of clinical outcomes in multi-parameter cytometry data
item.description: Cytometry-based prediction models often fail to generalise across patient cohorts. Here, the authors present dioscRi, a framework that enables interpretable prediction of clinical outcomes from immune cell populations across independent cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dynamic neuro-immune regulation of psychiatric risk loci in human neurons
item.description: Stress and inflammation influence the developing brain and are associated with mental health outcomes. Here the authors show that common genetic risk dynamically interacts with immune responses in human neurons.

item.title: Nature Communications: Umbrella-type stretchable electrode arrays for long-term neural recording
item.description: Stable recording of high-density neuronal ensembles at single-unit resolution over years-long timescales is challenging. Here, the authors develop umbrella-type stretchable electrode arrays anchored to surrounding brain tissue, forming a neuroelectronic interface that tracks the same neuronal ensembles in head-fixed mice over 1.5 years.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integration of GWAS and single-cell analysis for psoriasis identifies disease-associated cell subtypes and therapeutic targets
item.description: Integrating genetic data and skin single-cell data highlights psoriasis-associated cell types and cell type-specific functional mechanisms. These findings offer perspectives for identifying therapeutic targets for psoriasis at the cellular level.

item.title: Nature Communications: A dual A-to-Y and G-to-Y base editor and a four-base concurrent hypermutator in mammalian cells
item.description: Current base editors exhibit limited types of base conversion and constrained mutational diversity. Here the authors develop a dual base editor for A-to-Y and G-to-Y changes, and a quadruple base mutating module (QBMM) that mutates all four DNA bases in mammalian cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: In-silico solute transport via perivascular networks in the human intracranial space
item.description: This work introduces a multiscale, integrative modeling framework for brain fluid flow and solute transport, bridging mesoscale perivascular networks with the organ-level macroscale and timescales of seconds to hours in subject-specific geometries.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial analysis reveals cellular microenvironments and mechanisms of inflammation and injury in acute interstitial nephritis
item.description: Spatial analysis of human kidney biopsies reveals that acute interstitial nephritis differs from nonimmune kidney injury, identifying complement-producing injured tubules, T cell signaling and NAMPT as markers of sustained inflammatory niches.

item.title: Nature Communications: An FGF21-IGFBP1 tumor-liver relay drives musculoskeletal defects in colorectal cancer cachexia
item.description: Colorectal cancer often causes cachexia, a wasting syndrome that weakens muscles and bones. Here, the authors show that a tumor-liver signaling relay driven by FGF21 and IGFBP1 promotes this decline, identifying a potential target to preserve musculoskeletal health.

item.title: Nature Communications: A new core-genome MLST approach for Chlamydia trachomatis genomic surveillance and research
item.description: The use of whole-genome sequencing for classification and surveillance of the pathogen Chlamydia trachomatis is limited due to the lack of standardized typing frameworks. Here, the authors present a core-genome multilocus sequence typing system, accompanied by a hierarchical nomenclature, optimized for standardized local implementation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Small-molecule RAS/RAF inhibitors target RAS-driven cancers via allosteric RAF disruption
item.description: In this work authors identify small-molecule RAS/RAF inhibitors that bind an allosteric site in RAF, alter its structure, and suppress a broad range of RAS-driven cancers, including tumors that have become resistant to BRAF inhibitors.

item.title: Nature Communications: De novo E-cadherin/catenin complex formation controls basal epithelial mechanics and force transmission for apoptotic cell clearance
item.description: Epithelial cells remodel their shape during phagocytosis while preserving tissue cohesion. Here, authors show that the E-cadherin/catenin adhesion complex is repurposed at phagocytic contacts, where it controls mechanical forces essential for engulfment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cis glycan–glycan interactions organize membrane nanodomains that tune receptor signaling
item.description: Cell surfaces are coated with glycans, but how these sugars organize membranes and regulate receptors remains unclear. Here, authors show that direct glycan–glycan interactions form nanoscale ganglioside raft domains that restrain EGFR signaling

item.title: Nature Communications: The cortical microenvironment drives early immune organization and controls early osteoclastogenesis in bone healing
item.description: Here they identify a specialized cortical niche that coordinates immune and stromal cells to drive early osteoclast formation during fracture healing and show that aging primarily impairs this supportive microenvironment rather than the cells themselves.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD38-activated macrophages drive age-related placental senescence by depleting NAD + in decidual stromal cells
item.description: The authors show that CD38-activated macrophages deplete NAD+ in decidual stromal cells, driving placental senescence and fetal growth restriction during aging. NAD+ restoration in animal models improves pregnancy outcomes and offspring health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disitamab vedotin for HER2-positive breast cancer with liver metastases: phase 3 results from the RC48-C006 phase 2/3 trial
item.description: Patients with HER2-positive breast cancer with liver metastases (BCLM) have poor prognosis. Here, the authors report phase 3 results from the phase 2/3 RC48-C006 clinical trial comparing disitamab vedotin (HER2 targeted antibody drug conjugate) against lapatinib plus capecitabine in patients with HER2-postivie breast cancer with liver metastases previously treated with trastuzumab and taxanes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Risk factors for major depressive disorder among adults recruited from hospital settings in Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa
item.description: Across Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa, a harmonized study identified factors associated with major depression and found country differences explained 24% of variation, indicating regional strategies should be adapted to national contexts.

Nature Communications: Methylation Mesa define functional regulatory elements for targeted gene activation
item.description: DNA methylation influences gene expression, but the regulatory importance of specific methylated regions is unclear. Here, the authors identify “Methylation Mesa” as focal epigenetic regulatory elements and show that precise Mesa demethylation drives gene activation, chromatin remodeling and tumor suppression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Archipelago architecture and evolution of paclitaxel biosynthesis revealed by the Pseudotaxus chienii haplotype-resolved genome
item.description: Paclitaxel biosynthesis beyond Taxus has long been debated. Here, the authors report genome assembly of Pseudotaxus chienii and show that, while it retains a largely conserved genomic architecture for paclitaxel biosynthesis, extensive degradation of the terminal pathway suggests a substantial loss of paclitaxel-producing capacity.

item.title: Nature Communications: A bipartite glucan synthase-remodeler module organizes branched glucan assembly in the fungal cell wall
item.description: Fungal cell walls require glucan polymers to be synthesized and remodeled. Here, authors identify a synthase-remodeler pair that works together to build branched β-glucan and shape cell wall architecture.

item.title: Nature Communications: A redox switch on CDC48 regulates peroxisomal function via controlling peroxisome-associated protein degradation
item.description: Peroxisomes are essential for diverse biological functions. Here the authors show that H₂O₂‑triggered oxidation of the CDC48 AAA-ATPase complex in Arabidopsis regulates PEX22 abundance and fine-tunes peroxisomal activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Optotagging in primate cortex uncovers excitatory and inhibitory neuron specializations in form vision
item.description: This study leverages cell type-specific optogenetics in the monkey cerebral cortex to elucidate the unique functional contributions of excitatory and inhibitory neurons in visual form processing. The findings contribute to a more detailed mechanistic understanding of high-level vision in primates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Autoinhibition of untimely DNA binding by structural disorder in the full-length peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs)
item.description: Interdomain interactions by the disordered N-terminal region in PPAR transcription factors lead to autoinhibition of DNA binding. The effect is strongest for the monomer suggesting inhibition of untimely DNA binding prior to heterodimer formation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Circadian temperature compensation is intrinsically linked with metabolism and redox signaling
item.description: This study reveals that “temperature compensation,” a core defining property of circadian rhythms, links redox sensing of metabolism to modulation of the clock mechanism to preserve a constant circadian period under different temperatures in both bacterial and mammalian cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Triptolide sensitizes cancer cells to nucleoside DNA methyltransferase inhibitors through inhibition of DCTPP1-mediated cell-intrinsic resistance
item.description: Abnormal DNA hypermethylation is common in cancer, but DNA methyltransferase inhibitors show limited activity in many tumors. Here, the authors employ a chemical library screen to identify triptolide as an active agent that enhances these drugs by blocking DCTPP1, increasing drug incorporation into DNA, promoting demethylation and epigenetic reprogramming, and improving anti-cancer effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning aging marker from retinal images unveils sex-specific clinical and genetic signatures
item.description: Retinal images capture biological features of aging, but their links to health and disease are not fully understood. Here, the authors develop a retinal age predictor and show that accelerated retinal aging is associated with age‑related diseases, mortality and distinct sex‑specific genetic and biological signatures.

item.title: Nature Communications: A conserved small RNA-generating gene cluster undergoes sequence diversification and contributes to plant immunity
item.description: Here the authors reveal a conserved small RNA-producing gene cluster that undergoes sequence diversification, driving a co-evolutionary arms race with pathogens. This native innate immunity offers new opportunities to engineer disease resistance in plants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bi-directional highways and super-seeder tissues underpin parasite dissemination in experimental Leishmania donovani infection
item.description: Ecological analysis of murine Leishmania donovani infection reveals complex parasite within-host dynamics, with super-seeder sites fuelling dissemination between skin and viscera, and with key connections malleable after further immune perturbation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fusion-driven oncogenic programs shape the immune landscape in translocation renal cell carcinoma
item.description: Currently, there is limited understanding of the biology for translocation renal cell carcinoma (RCC), a rare RCC subtype defined by oncogenic TFE3 gene fusions. Here, the authors use multi-omics profiling to show that TFE3 fusions drive distinct tumor programs and an immunosuppressive microenvironment linked to reduced immunotherapy response.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Caenorhabditis elegans microbiome impacts microsporidia infection through nutrient limitation and spore inactivation
item.description: Here, the authors show that gut bacteria can protect nematodes from microsporidia via altering host fatty acids the parasites need to grow, and secreting molecules that inactivate parasite spores, revealing widespread bacterial impact on infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Atomic resolution structure of human papillomavirus bound to heparin
item.description: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant health burden, but the mechanisms of HPV receptor binding are not understood. Here, the authors solve a 1.9 Å resolution structure of HPV bound to heparin with insights into the binding interface.

item.title: Nature Communications: The cellular and molecular basis of gyrus-sulcus specialization in the primate brain
item.description: This study uncovers how differences in brain cell composition help define cortical folds and reveals a link between microscopic cellular organization and large-scale brain networks in primates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Peptides display multilayered hydration shell substructures dictated by sequence-specific surface chemistry
item.description: Water organization is central to how biomolecular structures function. Here, the authors use 3D-AFM to uncover sequence-specific multilayer hydration architectures around peptides, demonstrating how molecular surface chemistry shapes interfacial water structure.

item.title: Nature Communications: A machine-assisted framework for systematic error analysis in clinical concept extraction
item.description: MedError, a machine-assisted human-in-the-loop framework, improves the standardization, validity, and efficiency of clinical NLP error analysis, supporting more transparent and trustworthy model deployment.

item.title: Nature Communications: The dimensionality of plant–plant competition
item.description: Theory posits that competing species should occupy different niches to coexist, and this should be detectable in the interactions between them. In contrast, a new method indicates that plant-plant interactions show very limited niche differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: State-dependent binding of the wedge domain controls inactivation of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1
item.description: Inactivation of PIEZO1 in the presence of mechanical stimulation is essential for normal physiological function. Here, Roettger et al. show that the wedge domain binds to the flat conformation of PIEZO1 thereby stabilizing the flat state and controlling recovery from inactivation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell and in vivo profiling reveal heterogeneous and organ-specific CRISPR-Cas9 off-target and translocation outcomes
item.description: CRISPR can treat genetic disease, but unintended DNA changes remain a safety concern. Here, authors show that off-target editing and translocations vary widely between individual cells and organs, motivating the development of more sensitive and organ-specific safety assays for CRISPR therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Heritable transgenic schistosomes as a living platform for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody secretion
item.description: A heritable CRISPR knock-in in Schistosoma mansoni generated a transgenic line that secreted a functional anti–SARS-CoV-2 antibody into mouse circulation. Virus neutralization by infected mouse sera demonstrated a worm-based living biofoundry for sustained, in vivo biologic delivery.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cell autonomous regional differences in oligodendrocyte lineage development and responses to oncohistone H3.3 K27M
item.description: Here authors report that histone H3.3 K27M mutations drive diffuse midline glioma by ablating intrinsic regional differences in oligodendrocyte development, selectively expanding immature oligodendrocyte precursor cell populations in the brainstem while disrupting normal differentiation programs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Altered bone marrow niche forms central innate immune memory driving cardiac dysfunction
item.description: Heart failure has been shown to induce innate like memory responses in haematopoietic stem/progenitor cells and is linked to immunopathology. Here the authors show the formation of an altered bone marrow niche is linked to innate memory and cardiac dysfunction in heart failure.

item.title: Nature Communications: Human iPSC-cardiomyocyte-aggregate cell therapy in non-human primates and correlation of heart recovery with contractile and electrophysiological cardiomyocyte properties
item.description: The study shows successful therapy with hiPSC-cardiomyocyte aggregates in infarcted non-human primates, including uncoupling of cell production from transplantation and correlation of heart recovery in vivo with cardiomyocyte properties in vitro.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mucosal IgA to pre-fusion F protein predicts protection from RSV infection in a high burden setting
item.description: Hodgson et al present a longitudinal study of a Gambian community and report that antibodies in nasal fluid predict protection from Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infection better than those in blood, offering new insight to guide development of future RSV vaccines in high-burden settings.

item.title: Nature Communications: RTEL1 mutation modifies dyskeratosis congenita caused by a telomerase RNA template mutation
item.description: Telomere repeats are highly conserved, and disruptions in their maintenance can cause telomere disorders. Here, the authors identify a telomerase RNA mutation that generates variant telomeric repeats, reducing telomerase processivity and contributing to dyskeratosis congenita, with disease severity further influenced by RTEL1 variation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dual apical methyltransferases orchestrate motility initiation in apicomplexan parasites
item.description: This study identifies the Apicomplexa-specific methyltransferase PCKMT and reveals how it works with the previously known AKMT in a two-step pathway that initiates parasite motility and invasion.

item.title: Nature Communications: Leptomeningeal fibroblasts promote glioblastoma progression by regulating cerebrospinal fluid dynamics
item.description: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics are implicated in glioblastoma (GBM) pathogenesis and tumor microenvironment alterations. This study identifies leptomeningeal fibroblast–driven fibrosis as a contributing factor to impaired CSF clearance in GBM, linking it to immune suppression and therapeutic resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Novel surveillance design exploiting network analysis for efficient, rapid detection of emerging Clostridioides difficile strains
item.description: Using network analysis for inter-hospital spread and algorithmically optimising sentinel site selection, the authors design a surveillance system to rapidly detect emerging nosocomial pathogen strains within limited whole genome sequencing capacity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantifying replication fidelity of unnatural base pairs using nanopore sequencing
item.description: Expanded DNA alphabets with more than 4 letters can be replicated by polymerases, but with higher error rates than standard DNA. Here the authors develop a high-throughput sequencing approach to quantify the replication fidelity of unnatural base pairs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular determinants of species-specific gamete adhesion triggering HAP2-mediated membrane fusion
item.description: The molecular mechanisms linking gamete adhesion to membrane fusion are unknown. Here, the authors report the crystal structure of the complex between Chlamydomonas gamete adhesion proteins MAR1 and FUS1 and show that complex formation triggers fusogenic reconfiguration of conserved gamete fusion protein HAP2.

item.title: Nature Communications: Protein entanglement misfolding influences whether proteins undergo proteasomal degradation or persist in near-native misfolded states
item.description: Protein entanglements can generate long-lived misfolded states, but their cellular fate is poorly understood. Here, the authors combine proteomics and simulations to show that entanglement misfolding promotes proteasomal degradation, while soluble, near-native misfolded proteins escape degradation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Optimising antibiotic switching via forecasting of patient physiology
item.description: The authors present a decision support system that forecasts patients’ vital signs to identify those ready to switch from intravenous to oral antibiotics. Clinical criteria are applied to the forecasts to rank patients for stewardship review.

item.title: Nature Communications: Exosomal export of activated CASPASE-8 is linked to the prevention of TNF-induced cytotoxicity
item.description: The ESCRT machinery and the chaperone HSC70 package activated CASP8 into intralumenal vesicles preventing TNF-induced apoptosis. Microbial effector proteins interfere with this detoxification mechanism and sensitize cells to TNF cytotoxicity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Leveraging long read RNA-seq to decipher neuronal regulation of alternative polyadenylation
item.description: Long-read RNA sequencing enables precise mapping of RNA 3′ ends. Here, the authors develop APALORD, a computational framework for high-resolution alternative polyadenylation analysis that uncovers a preference for stronger polyadenylation site selection during neural differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mutant TP53 hijacks RNA-splicing factor RBM28 to suppress double-stranded RNA triggered antitumor immunity
item.description: Mutant p53 (mutp53) drives tumor immune evasion partly through restricting innate immune sensing triggered by transposable elements (TEs). Here, the authors find that mutations in the DNA-binding domain enable mutp53 to transcriptionally activate the RNA-splicing factor RBM28, leading to excessive splicing of TE transcripts and suppression of antitumor immunity in esophageal cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Divergent SAGA complexes shape the Toxoplasma transcriptome for lytic cycle progression and host interaction
item.description: Researchers show that the zoonotic parasite Toxoplasma gondii built a unique chromatin modifying complex to activate the genes that drive infection and virulence, revealing a potential weak spot for new treatments.

item.title: Nature Communications: BRANCHED1 acts as a rheostat of Nuclear Factor Y-dependent epigenetic regulation in axillary bud development
item.description: Shoot branching plasticity is largely regulated by BRC1. The authors show that BRC1 acts as a dose-dependent rheostat, modulating NF-Y-mediated chromatin looping and H3K27me3 demethylation at floral organ development genes to fine-tune axillary bud activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ectoderm tensile stress controls mesoderm internalization during embryo gastrulation
item.description: The biomechanical basis for tissue folding during morphogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here they show that precisely balanced mechanical tension in tissues surrounding the future mesoderm is essential for its internalization during fruit fly gastrulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular basis of diverse ligand recognition and species-specific pharmacology at the complement anaphylatoxin receptor C3aR
item.description: The complement anaphylatoxin receptor, C3aR is a potential drug target in various inflammatory disorders. Here, authors present insights into its activation, signaling, and pharmacology that is likely to facilitate therapeutic design going forward.

item.title: Nature Communications: An atlas of colonization factors in the human gut microbiome reveals ecological strategies and inflammatory bowel disease signatures
item.description: Here, Meng et al. establish a human gut microbiome atlas of colonization factors, revealing distinct ecological strategies used by microbes to persist in the intestine, and show that inflammatory bowel disease is associated with remodeling of colonization-associated functions and microbial carriers.

item.title: Nature Communications: The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome
item.description: The molecular function of many mitochondrial proteins remains unknown. Here, the authors present MitoMatch, an AlphaFold Multimer-based compendium of mitochondrial protein interactions that links orphan proteins to known pathways, defines the CoQ metabolon, and reveals the role of COA4 in copper delivery to cytochrome c oxidase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Causal inference for multiple risk factors and diseases from genomics data
item.description: Mendelian randomization aims to identify causal relationships from genetic data, but results can be biased by confounding. Here, the authors develop CI-GWAS, a statistical framework that improves causal inference and shows that many suspected risk factor-disease associations in UK Biobank may reflect unmeasured confounding.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fibrin-rich environment drives catheter-associated UTIs by suppressing macrophage defenses
item.description: Marrufo et al. show that fibrinolytic deficiency resulting in extravascular fibrin formation in the bladder predisposes hosts to CAUTIs and systemic dissemination by modulating macrophages’ bactericidal response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Maternal obesity programs offspring metabolic dysfunction via small extracellular vesicle-mediated epigenetic remodeling
item.description: The study identifies a transplacental sEV–miRNA–epigenetic axis as a mediator of maternal obesity. Maternal plasma sEVs transfer miR-29a-3p to the fetal liver, epigenetically reprogramming glucose metabolism and driving adult insulin resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Redox-stratified macromolecule degradation supports microbial survival in the oligotrophic Kermadec Trench sediments
item.description: Understanding how microbes survive in the crushing pressure and nutrient-poor conditions of the deepest ocean has remained a major challenge. This study reveals that Kermadec Trench microbes thrive by recycling organic matter and flexibly switching energy-generation pathways.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-source agent-based modeling to optimize influenza mitigation strategies in Hong Kong
item.description: Modeling six influenza seasons to evaluate mitigation strategies, this study proposes a signal-responsive policy framework. Findings show child vaccination and mask use curb transmission; their combination is vital during vaccine mismatches.

item.title: Nature Communications: Substrate curvature and stiffness equivalence in governing cell mechanosensing
item.description: This study reveals how cells translate substrate stiffness and curvature into biological responses through focal adhesion tilting, uncovering a mechanical equivalence that opens new routes for designing cell-instructive biomaterials.

item.title: Nature Communications: SPOP-mediated ZMYND8 ubiquitination and phase separation exclusion drives mTOR inhibitor resistance in kidney cancer
item.description: Resistance to mTOR inhibitors is common in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) patients. The authors show that the histone reader ZMYND8 undergoes ubiquitination, disrupting its phase separation and promoting its recruitment into a transcriptional activator complex with ZHX2, which leads to mTOR-independent activation of p70S6K and drug resistance in preclinical ccRCC models

item.title: Nature Communications: Therapeutic modulation of the vitreoretinal fibrosis microenvironment in female mice using engineered macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles
item.description: Vitreoretinal fibrosis is a hallmark of proliferative vitreoretinopathy, a severe blinding disease that necessitates surgery. Here, the authors show that engineered extracellular vesicles therapeutically modulate this microenvironment to effectively inhibit fibrosis and prevent further retinal detachment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Time-dependent bistability leads to critical slowing down during floral transition in Arabidopsis
item.description: Developmental transitions such as the switch to flowering are fundamental processes in multicellular organisms, yet their underlying regulatory dynamics remain incompletely understood. This study demonstrates that floral transition at the Arabidopsis shoot apical meristem is governed by a time-dependent bistable switch involving the floral inhibitor APETALA2 and floral activators, revealing critical slowing dynamics, transient ghost attractors, and a mechanism that explains observed variability and robustness across genotypes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combinatorial group testing for efficient scaling across biological applications
item.description: Combinatorial group testing can reduce experimental costs but remains challenging to apply due to its complexity and the lack of implementation tools. Here, the authors present PoolPy, a complete combinatorial group testing framework, enabling up to 93% cost reduction across biological assays.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functional immune changes are conserved in COVID-19 and trauma patients receiving intensive care
item.description: In this prospective cohort study, the authors conduct a longitudinal comparison of innate immune cell function and plasma protein expression, revealing shared immune alterations between two distinct critical illnesses, COVID-19 infection and trauma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Next-generation multiplexed targeted proteomics quantifies post-translational modifications in disease and compound-protein interactions with high throughput
item.description: Targeted multiplexed proteomic technologies enable quantification of target proteins without prior assay development. Here, the authors describe improvements enabling quantification of site-specific modifications, including post-translational modifications and covalent compound-protein interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Predicting acute and chronic diabetes complications among adults newly diagnosed with diabetes: development and validation of dynamic risk prediction models
item.description: Here the researchers developed novel machine learning models that use routine clinical data to predict the risks of the nine common acute and chronic diabetes complications with predictions that update dynamically as new clinical data become available, with validation across two independent U.S. healthcare populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unc-51 like kinase 3 (ULK3) contributes to autophagy and cell survival in multiple myeloma
item.description: Autophagy-related mechanisms in multiple myeloma (MM) remains to be understood. Here the authors find that ULK3 contributes to autophagy and supports MM cell survival, calling for future development of more selective ULK3-directed therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Actin based cell chirality emerging at the boundary of 2D-microtissue directs chiral multicellular pattern formation
item.description: Based on chiral self-organisation of actin fibres in confined cells of varied shapes, a model for cell alignment in 2D microtissues was validated, in which cell chirality emerges at boundaries and propagates inward, guiding multicellular chirality.

item.title: Nature Communications: Load-dependent RGD-context sensing via αV-class integrins reprograms cell adhesion and mechanics
item.description: Here the authors show that αV-class integrins distinguish the RGD motif of vitronectin from other ligands and, within seconds, deploy β-subunit-specific, load-dependent programs in which αVβ3 and αVβ5 cooperate to tune fibroblast adhesion and mechanics to ECM composition.

item.title: Nature Communications: TOR–NOT4 signalling couples translation to co-translational quality control in plants
item.description: Here, Schwarze et al. reveal how plant cells match protein quality control to changing rates of protein production through a functional link between TOR kinase signalling and NOT4 E3 ubiquitin ligases

item.title: Nature Communications: Dynamic hinge-motion of PfRIPR revealed by malaria invasion inhibitory antibodies
item.description: The PfPCRCR complex is essential for invasion of human erythrocytes by the malaria parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. Here, authors structurally and functionally characterise antibodies’ interactions with PfPCRCR, with implications for the design of PfRIPR-based anti-malarial vaccines.

item.title: Nature Communications: A transmembrane protein confers the Yr26 / Yr24 / YrCH42 / YrG22 -mediated stripe rust resistance in wheat
item.description: Yellow rust (YR) is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Here, the authors report the cloning of Yr26 as a transmembrane protein and reveal its evolves within the Triticeae lineage as an orphan gene.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mitochondrial SUMOylation of NDUFA9 drives ClpP-dependent degradation and complex I dysfunction in a Leigh syndrome–associated mutation
item.description: The Leigh syndrome–associated R321P mutation drives excessive SUMOylation of NDUFA9, promoting ClpP-dependent degradation, weakening mitochondrial complex I, and causing mitochondrial and motor dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transposon end recognition and excision mechanisms of type I-F CRISPR-associated transposases
item.description: CRISPR-associated transposons mediate RNA-guided DNA integration, but the molecular basis of transposase function remains poorly understood. Here, the authors uncover the mechanism of a highly active type I-F transposase, informing the engineering of programmable DNA insertion tools.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fossil record biases skew inferences of mammal trait evolution
item.description: Fossils document the evolution of life on Earth but represent only a small fraction of the species that ever existed. This study illustrates how common fossil record biases can render a distorted picture of past communities’ composition and change.

item.title: Nature Communications: Maternal Huluwa regulates postfertilization microtubule array organization for asymmetrical transport of dorsal determinants in zebrafish
item.description: Here they show that maternal Huluwa protein localizes at the zebrafish egg’s vegetal pole, organizing postfertilization microtubules to transport dorsal determinants and establishing the body axis through a dual-phase mechanism.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mesoscale proximity labeling at chromatin leads to identification of small molecule mechanism of action
item.description: The authors develop MesoMap, an extension of their previous proximity labeling system, which uses multiple baits on labeled histones to measure changes across chromatin rather than to a single specific protein.

item.title: Nature Communications: The anion channel GPR89 is a tumor-specific dependency in breast cancer
item.description: Oncogene-driven endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is common in cancer. Here, authors show breast cancers extend Golgi anion channel GPR89 to the ER to mitigate this stress, creating a potentially targetable dependency and new therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Larger habitat islands maintain more persistent mutualistic assemblages
item.description: Habitat loss can disrupt mutualistic interactions that sustain biodiversity. This study shows that larger habitat islands support more persistent plant-frugivore and plant-pollinator assemblages, linked to network modularity and nestedness.

item.title: Nature Communications: GNL3 SUMOylation is essential for DNA double-strand break repair by homologous recombination
item.description: GNL3 is identified as a key regulator of DNA repair, where its SUMOylation enables interaction with the BLM-DNA2 complex to promote DNA end resection and homologous recombination. Targeting this pathway sensitizes cancer cells to therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: iEVIP: a dual-inspired intelligent platform for smart response extracellular vesicle isolation and single-vesicle profiling
item.description: Extracellular vesicle analysis is hindered by membrane fouling during isolation and vesicle aggregation during imaging. Here, authors introduce iEVIP, a platform combining pulsatile filtration, nanoscale sample organization and machine learning for high-throughput single-vesicle analysis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Compartmentalized B cell-microglia crosstalk drives ischemic white matter demyelination
item.description: The role of B cells in vascular cognitive impairment is unclear. Here, the authors show a crosstalk between CNS border-associated B cells and parenchymal microglia, through MIFCD74/CXCR4 and IgG signaling, exacerbating white matter injury.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tunable and self-reporting esterase-activated cyanide prodrugs exert cytoprotective effects
item.description: Hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is traditionally regarded as a highly toxic industrial pollutant, but growing evidence suggests that, at low concentrations, it can act as an endogenous signaling molecule with gasotransmitter-like properties. Here, the authors develop a series of esterase-activated cyanide donors featuring tunable release kinetics and concomitant fluorophore generation, enabling self-reporting cyanide delivery through fluorescence. As a key result, the optimized donor Et-1 displayed therapeutic activity in a mouse ischemia–reperfusion model, achieving efficacy at doses as low as 0.3 mg kg⁻¹.

item.title: Nature Communications: Supporting upper limb movements with a soft robot after a brachial plexus injury
item.description: Brachial plexus injury causes severe arm weakness, forcing patients to rely on compensatory movements for daily activities. Here, the authors develop an exosuit for shoulder and elbow assistance and demonstrate its ability to improve arm movement, reduce effort, and support daily tasks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preserved topography, lateralization, selectivity, and functional connectivity of the language network in older brains
item.description: Here, the authors show that aging affects brain networks differently, with neural changes mirroring the preservation or decline of the cognitive functions they support. The multiple demand network exhibits age-related decline while the language network remains stable with age.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cohesin acts as a transcriptional gatekeeper by restraining pause–release to promote processive elongation
item.description: Tei et al. show that cohesin regulates transcription in human cells by maintaining active promoter states and ensuring sufficient Pol II pausing, thereby promoting orderly entry into productive elongation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma metabolomic signatures enable the diagnosis and prognosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
item.description: This study combines plasma metabolomics and machine learning to identify blood biomarkers that improve the diagnosis, classification and prognosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, supporting earlier detection and more precise patient care.

item.title: Nature Communications: A wearable acoustofluidic patch for rapid reversal of opioid overdose
item.description: Opioid overdose can be deadly, and timely naloxone delivery remains challenging. Here, the authors develop a wearable acoustofluidic patch that detects overdose using deep-learning respiratory sensing and automatically delivers naloxone to reverse fentanyl overdose in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: An LRR-truncated NLR natural variant confers dual resistance to drought and blast in rice
item.description: Genetic resources with combined resistance to drought and blast disease are scarce. Here, the authors identify NLR8 - Hap2, a natural allele of the rice NLR gene NLR8 that encodes an LRR-truncated protein, and show that it enhances resistance to both stresses by stabilizing two distinct transcription factors.

item.title: Nature Communications: XPO1-mediated TRIM21 nuclear export reprograms TREM2+ macrophage polarization by targeting IRF3 to augment anti-PD-1 efficacy in small cell lung cancer
item.description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) resistant to Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, the authors define an XPO1-TRIM21-TNFSF15 axis that promotes the polarization of immunosuppressive TREM2+ macrophages, which ultimately orchestrates immune exclusion by impairing antigen presentation. Importantly, targeting XPO1 enhances the efficacy of anti-PD1 immunotherapy in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Risk of Tuberculosis in Type 2 Diabetes
item.description: A large international study found that certain diabetes drugs (GLP-1 receptor agonists) may link to a lower risk of tuberculosis than other common treatments. These medications may offer added protection against tuberculosis in type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal digital phenotyping of activity rhythms and biological aging using commercial wearables
item.description: Long-term links between free-living rest-activity rhythms and biological aging remain unclear. Here, the authors show that Fitbit-derived rest-activity rhythms are associated with biological aging trajectories in All of Us Research Program.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tirzepatide versus GLP-1 receptor agonists and stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation and type 2 diabetes
item.description: Among adults with atrial fibrillation and type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide use was associated with lower risks of stroke and death than other GLP-1 receptor agonists. The findings support trials of its cerebrovascular benefits in this high-risk group.

item.title: Nature Communications: Alcohol reshapes liver zonal plasticity and immune-metabolic reprogramming in metabolic-syndrome associated hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Alcohol consumption and high fat diet can drive liver cancer through distinct pathways. Here, the authors characterize three murine models of steatohepatitis-associated hepatocarcinogenesis that recapitulate metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), alcohol-related liver disease (ALD), and their overlapped condition, MetALD, showing that alcohol reshapes liver zonal plasticity and β-catenin-AhR signaling to alter tumor origin and increase immunotherapy sensitivity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic architecture of cytokine autoantibodies and associated risk of common diseases
item.description: Despite limited understanding of cytokine autoantibodies, this study reveals a heterogeneous genetic architecture, with distinct profiles conferring reduced risk of certain cancers and rheumatoid arthritis, but increased susceptibility to diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Zanidatamab in patients with early stage HER2-positive breast cancer: the NeoZanHER phase 2 single-arm open-label trial
item.description: With the improvement of HER2-targeted therapy in patients with breast cancer, there is growing interest in whether chemotherapy can be eliminated from regimens completely. Here, the authors report a phase 2 clinical trial investigating neoadjuvant zanidatamab (HER2-targeting antibody) in patients with early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Haemodynamic control of zonated liver function via instructive vascular Wnt signalling
item.description: The study identified blood flow as the key signal that programs liver blood vessels to instruct liver function through WNT signalling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plan-related inequalities in costs, disease progression and mortality among hypertensive patients in China
item.description: An analysis of 8 million hypertension-related hospital admissions in China shows that health insurance payment plans are linked to costs, disease progression and survival, revealing gaps in financial protection and access to care.

item.title: Nature Communications: 18 Month patency of acellular bioengineered regenerative conduit as coronary artery bypass
item.description: Here the authors tested lab-grown blood vessels as heart bypass grafts in sheep, adding an external support to prevent kinking. The vessels stayed open for 18 months, even after blood thinners were stopped, while transforming into living, functional tissue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Improving early prediction for adverse dengue outcomes using data from the IDAMS prospective multicentre study
item.description: Authors used laboratory tests and clinical symptoms to predict dengue progression in a multi-country study. Prediction models improved in accuracy over time, enabling earlier admission of high-risk patients without overwhelming hospital capacity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning for precision grading of Schistosoma japonicum -induced liver fibrosis in ultrasound images
item.description: Researchers developed a deep learning system that accurately grades schistosomiasis-related liver fibrosis from ultrasound, and deployed it on Windows and Android devices to support consistent screening and follow-up in endemic regions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gestational age modifies associations between Group B Streptococcus genomic characteristics and postnatal age at disease onset
item.description: This Danish study shows that gestational age modifies the association between Group B Streptococcus genomic characteristics and postnatal age at disease onset in infants. The findings may help inform surveillance and maternal vaccination strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: An endometrial immune atlas across the female menstrual cycle reveals lymphoid aggregates compromise pregnancy
item.description: The immune landscape of human endometrium is remodeled across the menstrual cycle. The authors here provide a comprehensive immune atlas of these changes, and show that ectopic lymphoid aggregates, composed of germinal-center-B-like cells and T follicular helper-like cells, form in mouse and human chronic endometritis, which might lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex-specific trajectories of nonlinear immune aging at single-cell level
item.description: A multi-ethnic study of immune cells from 1,828 individuals finds that men and women age nonlinearly and differently at the cellular level. This work reveals sex-specific pathways and proposes personalized approaches to immune aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: Six-compound cocktail for maturation of human pluripotent stem cell-derived liver spheroids for toxicity prediction
item.description: This study reports a defined cocktail that matures human iPSC-derived hepatocytes to transcriptionally and functionally mimic primary hepatocytes, enabling personalized drug toxicity prediction and recapitulation of key fatty liver disease features.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic licensing of quiescent glioblastoma activation and immune evasion via astrocyte-mitochondria shuttle
item.description: Reactivation of quiescent cells at the invasive margin of glioblastoma tumors does not trigger an efficient immune elimination and these tumours tend to disseminate and recur even with therapy. Here the authors describe a metabolic regulatory pathway involving transfer of mitochondria enriched with the one‑carbon metabolism enzyme SHMT2, which cargo reactivates quiescent glioblastoma cells via metabolic regulation of mRNA methylation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular heterogeneity and clonal origin of CCR8 + effector regulatory T cells in human cancer
item.description: Studies of conserved molecular programs in regulatory T cells (Tregs) across human tumors are limited. Here, by integrating scRNAseq datasets from 9 tumor types, the authors identify a common signature of human Treg cells across solid tumors, further dissecting the molecular and functional heterogeneity of human intratumoral Tregs.

item.title: Nature Communications: A systematic review and meta-analysis on heat thresholds for maternal health and birth outcomes
item.description: Pregnant individuals can be particularly vulnerable to environmental heat exposure. Here, the authors report a systematic review and meta-analysis that identifies temperature thresholds associated with increasing risks of adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: ALPaCA: Adapting Llama for Pathology Context Analysis to enable slide-level question answering
item.description: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) have revolutionised computational pathology, but still struggle with the analysis of pyramidal, gigapixel-scale whole-slide images (WSIs). Here, the authors introduce ALPaCA (Adapting Llama for Pathology Context Analysis), a general-purpose slide-level LVLM designed for WSI analysis and question answering across a broad range of cancer types and tissue sites.

item.title: Nature Communications: Drug screen and machine learning predict neuroprotective agents in a preclinical human model of childhood dementia
item.description: Here authors show patient-derived neural models of childhood dementia exhibit key disease features. A drug screening platform integrating machine learning, imaging, transcriptomics and electrophysiology, identifies repurposed compounds that mitigate adverse effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: Advancing human-centric AI for robust X-ray analysis through holistic self-supervised learning
item.description: In this study, Moutakanni and colleagues introduce RayDINO, a self-supervised chest X-ray foundation model trained on 840,000 images, that outperforms supervised methods across nine radiology tasks and shows improved generalization and reduced bias across demographics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diagnostic performance and antibiotic impact of droplet digital PCR in suspected sepsis: the PROGRESS trial
item.description: In a multicenter randomized trial of patients with suspected sepsis, droplet digital PCR identified bloodstream pathogens faster and more often than blood culture and guided earlier, better-targeted antibiotics linked to improved survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clonal sharing and plasticity of follicular CD4 + T cells across lymph nodes and tumors in non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: To provide additional insights into the biology of CD4 + T cells in cancer, here the authors report a multi-omics analysis of CD4 + T cells from matched blood, tumor invaded lymph nodes (LNs), and tumor tissues of patients with non-small cell lung cancer, showing that tumor-invaded LNs and tumors harbor clonally linked and plastic follicular CD4+T cell subsets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Blood-brain barrier-penetrant nanotherapy inhibits haem oxygenase-1-mediated ferroptosis for post-resuscitation neuroprotection
item.description: Limited drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) hinders the therapy of post-resuscitation brain injury after cardiac arrest. Here, the authors report zwitterionic poly (tertiary amine oxide)-based micelles that cross the BBB via transcytosis and deliver artesunate to suppress haem oxygenase-1-driven ferroptosis, restore iron homeostasis and provide neuroprotection after resuscitation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Associations of loneliness, social isolation and healthy lifestyle with life expectancy free of major physical disease and mental disorder
item.description: The authors observe that loneliness and social isolation relate to shorter life expectancy free of physical (type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, neurodegenerative disease, and cancer) and mental disorders (depression and anxiety) in the UK Biobank. These associations are particularly pronounced for mental disorders, and the loss of disease-free life expectancy associated with social isolation is attenuated in individuals with healthier lifestyles.

item.title: Nature Communications: Impact of the anti-inflammatory macrolide glasmacinal on the gut microbiota of healthy adults: an open-label trial
item.description: Here, in a clinical trial in healthy participants, the authors show that glasmacinal, an oral macrolide with immunomodulatory properties, exerts limited changes to the gut microbiome and does select for antimicrobial resistance, unlike conventional antibiotics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bispecific chimeric autoantibody receptor T cells eliminate acetylcholine receptor-specific B cells in myasthenia gravis models
item.description: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder mediated by autoantibodies targeting the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. Here, the authors engineered chimaeric autoantibody receptor T cells that reduced pathogenic autoantibody titres and IgG deposition in a mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma proteomics defines two reproducible subphenotypes of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury with distinct outcomes
item.description: Sepsis is a leading cause of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients and carries a high risk of death, yet its biology varies between patients. Here, the authors show that plasma proteomics defines two subtypes with distinct outcomes and drug response, identified by a seven-protein test.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modelling anti-Ov16 seroprevalence for the control and elimination of onchocerciasis
item.description: Ov16 antibody tests are used for onchocerciasis surveillance. Fitting a transmission model to age-stratified seroprevalence data identified patent infection as the most likely parasite stage leading to seropositivity, indicating ongoing transmission.

item.title: Nature Communications: HMGA1-HP1β axis regulates premature aging in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome through chromatin remodeling
item.description: Premature aging disorders and normal aging involve changes in chromatin, but the key regulators are not fully understood. Here, the authors show HMGA1 stabilizes HP1β to remodel chromatin, curb cellular aging and extend lifespan in a progeria mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Locus-specific stratification and prioritization unveil genetic risk mechanism underlying complex diseases
item.description: Genetic risk of complex diseases poses unique challenges. Here, the authors develop a locus-specific stratification and gene regulatory prioritisation strategy to address issues arising from multi-signals in complex diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global genomic surveillance uncovers emergence and spatiotemporal patterns of World Health Organization priority antibiotic resistance in invasive Salmonella
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance in invasive Salmonella is an escalating global health threat, yet its global trends and genomic evidence remain poorly understood. Wang and Xu et al . use a state-of-the-art pipeline integrating global genomics to reveal emergence and spatiotemporal patterns of WHO priority antibiotic resistance in invasive Salmonella .

item.title: Nature Communications: Tracking funding disparities in global health aid with machine learning
item.description: Misalignment between health aid and country-level disease burden can leave populations without the necessary support for major health challenges. Here the authors report a machine learning analysis of global health aid and conclude that aid is often misaligned with country-level disease burden, with non-communicable diseases receiving limited aid despite their large global burden.

item.title: Nature Communications: Measurable residual disease detected by next-generation sequencing in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
item.description: The clinical value of next-generation sequencing for measurable residual disease (NGS-MRD) monitoring in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia remains to be fully established. Tracking TCR rearrangements in pediatric patients, this study shows that NGS-MRD serves as a useful method to stratify outcomes and identifies high-risk cases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Engineered bacteria as exogenous organelle mimics restore PTEN and p53 tumor suppressor functions for cancer therapy
item.description: PTEN and p53 are two of the most frequently mutated or inactivated tumor suppressor genes. Here, the authors engineer Salmonella to act as exogenous organelle-like devices that deliver PTEN and an MDM2 inhibitor to reactivate p53 to tumors, achieving durable tumor suppression and synergistic immune activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A viral-based individualized neoantigen vaccine as adjuvant treatment in resected head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a randomized Phase I trial
item.description: Patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) have limited sensitivity to immunotherapies. The authors report the development of TG4050, a modified vaccinia Ankara (MVA) virus-based individualized neoantigen vaccine, here tested in a randomized phase I trial as adjuvant treatment in patients with resected HNSCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intracellular artificial DNA receptor-loaded gelated cells for aflatoxin theranostics
item.description: The mycotoxin Aflatoxin B1 is highly toxic to human beings. Here, Li and co-workers report that engineered cell particles carrying aflatoxin aptamers can be used to both detect and eliminate Aflatoxin B1, in vitro and in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: PD-1 regulates CD4 + T cell-mediated CD8 + T cell responses in the brain to balance viral control and neuroinflammation
item.description: JC polyomavirus infection can result in progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, and T cells have been shown to express PD-1. Here the authors show that PD-1 regulates the CD4 + T cell mediated CD8 + T cell response in the brain regulating the antiviral response and neuroinflammation in a mouse polyomavirus central nervous system infection model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sintilimab plus Bevacizumab biosimilar IBI305 and chemotherapy as a first-line treatment in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (SBAGA): a single-arm, phase Ib/II study
item.description: Previous evaluations on anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody indicate its therapeutic potential in gastric cancer treatment. Here this group reports a phase Ib/II trial combining sintilimab/bevacizumab biosimilar IBI305/CapeOX chemotherapy as the first-line treatment on 54 patients with HER2-negative advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD36-mediated lipid-accumulation in reactive microglia contributes to retinal degeneration via the NLRP3-IL-1β pathway in mice
item.description: Metabolic stress can reshape immune cells into drivers of tissue damage. This study identifies CD36-driven lipid accumulation in reactive microglia as a mechanism linking retinal inflammation to degeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bidirectional associations between loneliness and physical multimorbidity and the mediating role of social inactivity
item.description: Both multimorbidity and loneliness are major public health issues. Here, the authors show that physical multimorbidity and loneliness are bidirectionally linked and social inactivity partially mediates the pathway from physical multimorbidity to loneliness.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide pQTL mapping in human skin identifies specific genetic regulators and mechanistic links to skin disorders
item.description: This study creates a genetic map of protein regulation in human skin, identifying genetic regulators of protein abundance and candidate disease-related proteins linked to leprosy, atopic dermatitis and psoriasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phosphorylation of OTUB1 promotes autophagy initiation under starvation
item.description: This study uncovers a phosphorylation-dependent regulatory mechanism controlling OTUB1’s function in nutrient deficiency-triggered autophagy initiation, providing cellular and molecular evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of fasting in alleviating MASLD.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo labeling–based proteomic analysis of early follicle oocytes and cisplatin-induced alterations in mice
item.description: Using in situ APEX labeling, this study maps proteins and RNA in mouse oocytes from early ovarian follicles and shows how cisplatin alters these cells, identifying EZH2 inhibition as a potential strategy to lessen cisplatin-induced oocyte damage.

item.title: Nature Communications: DUSP4 promotes anti-tumor CD8 + T cell function and boosts CAR-T cell efficacy in mouse colorectal cancer
item.description: Dual-specificity phosphatases (DUSPs) regulate cellular signaling pathways by dephosphorylating protein residues, which also modulates CD8 + T cell signaling. Here, the authors investigate the role of DUSP4 in AOM/DSS-induced colorectal cancer, finding DUSP4 to enhance T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity via ERK2-KLF2 signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Safety and immunogenicity of inactivated human Rotavirus vaccine in young children and infants: a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase I clinical trial
item.description: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose escalation phase I trial evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of an inactivated rotavirus vaccine (IRV) in healthy young children and infants without prior rotavirus vaccination or HIV infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tubular ACSM3 controls fatty acid metabolism and safeguards against acute kidney injury in male mice
item.description: Fatty acid oxidation impairment represents a hallmark of acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors report that tubular deficiency of ACSM3, an enzyme involved in medium chain fatty acid activation, is protective against kidney injury in male mouse models of AKI potentially via modulating PPARα activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: AAT/ SERPINA1 Pi*Z variant linked to gestational length and preterm birth prevention via AAT in mice
item.description: Preterm birth affects around 10% of pregnancies and lacks effective preventive therapies. Here, the authors identify the SERPINA1 PiZ variant as a genetic risk factor for shorter gestational duration and show that alpha‑1‑antitrypsin supplementation protects against inflammation‑induced preterm birth in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-ancestry genetic architecture of heart failure subtypes
item.description: This study maps the genetic basis of major heart failure subtypes across diverse populations, identifying shared and subtype-specific risk variants that may inform biology, risk prediction and future therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Commensal bacteria inhibit viral infections via a tryptophan metabolite
item.description: Previous studies suggest that commensal bacteria modulate viral infections. Here, the authors use HIV as a model to show that commensal bacteria impact viral infections, pinpointing a specific tryptophan metabolite as a key player.

item.title: Nature Communications: The transmission-blocking dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum sexual-stage antibody responses in a six-year cohort of Ugandan children and adults
item.description: The study found that naturally acquired immunity that reduces malaria transmission was rare but persistent in a minority of individuals. Transmission reduction was associated with antibodies against gametocyte proteins and with recent parasite exposure.

item.title: Nature Communications: Peritoneal ovarian cancer growth in the omentum proceeds independently of mature adipocytes
item.description: Ovarian cancer (OC) often spreads to the omentum, an adipose-rich tissue in the abdomen. Here, authors show that FABP4-expressing endothelial cells contribute to OC growth in the omentum independently of mature adipocytes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Amiloride mitigates respiratory distress caused by WFDC2 deficiency via inhibiting the epithelial sodium channel
item.description: This study identifies a WFDC2 mutation that causes a severe cystic-fibrosis-like airway disease in humans and mice. The mutation overactivates the epithelial sodium channel, and treatment with the drug amiloride improves survival and lung function in affected mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A foundation model for acute abdomen diagnosis stratification and triage on noncontrast computed tomography
item.description: The authors present AbdomenNet, a foundation model for non-contrast computed tomography. It detects 11 acute abdominal conditions, helps identify high-risk cases, improves radiologist accuracy, and may speed emergency reporting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale admixture mapping in the All of Us Research Program improves the characterization of cross-population phenotypic differences
item.description: In this work, Mandla et al. identified >50 genetic loci where ancestry was associated with a trait, expanding on the underlying biological mechanisms of these traits and the potential genetic factors of their differences between populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: IL-2 mutein-engrafted antibody MHS552 selectively expands functional regulatory T cells in nonclinical models and healthy participants
item.description: Although low-dose IL-2 therapy has shown promise in treating autoimmune and inflammatory conditions by supporting the expansion and immunosuppressive activity of regulatory T cells (Treg), robust clinical responses have been lacking. Here, the authors describe the design of the Treg-selective IL-2 agonist MHS552, its preclinical characterization in non-human primates, and a first-in-human dose escalation study in healthy participants reporting efficacy, selectivity and safety of the IL-2 mutein.

item.title: Nature Communications: Population-based genomic detection of childhood cancer predisposition using newborn dried blood spots
item.description: Prospective genomic newborn screening in large populations with extended follow-ups are necessary to assess the impact of the inclusion of cancer genes on outcomes. Here, the authors show that newborn screening for germline cancer risk, using a limited panel of cancer predisposition genes, would identify the approximately 1/27,000 babies who will develop a cancer in the first eight years of life due to a cancer predisposition syndrome, including nearly all children who go on to develop bilateral retinoblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neutrophil extracellular traps promote liver metastasis by impairing NK cell-dependent tumor surveillance via CCDC25
item.description: The formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contributes to liver metastasis and immune suppression. Here the authors show that NET-derived DNA can be sensed by CCDC25 on natural killer (NK) cells impairing NK cell-dependent tumor surveillance and promoting liver metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic conditions and aortic disease risk: a prospective cohort study with predictive and etiological analyses
item.description: This study shows that multimorbidity and several chronic conditions, including cardiovascular, respiratory and kidney diseases, are associated with higher risk of aortic disease in two large cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Noninvasive 3D mapping of tissue stress using reverberant shear wave
item.description: Mechanical stress shapes soft tissue health, but imaging it non-invasively in vivo has remained a challenge. Here, authors used physics-informed MRI wave analysis to map 3D tissue stress, enabling non-invasive intracranial pressure and tumor-induced stress estimates in brain tumor patients.

item.title: Nature Communications: Th17 effector cytokines induce shared and distinct microglial and endothelial cell responses in a mouse model for post-streptococcal encephalitis
item.description: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) infections can cause neuropsychiatric symptoms in children, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that IL-17A–IL17RA signaling in microglia mediates blood brain barrier dysfunction and neuroinflammation after GAS infection in a mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Blood metabolomic signatures linking air pollution to lung cancer in the Cancer Prevention Studies
item.description: Exposure to ambient air pollution is an established risk factor for lung cancer. In here, the authors report multiple metabolic perturbations that may mediate the association between ambient air pollution exposure and lung cancer risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pseudomonas aeruginosa -derived volatile organic compounds modulate AhR signaling to dysregulate airway mucus homeostasis
item.description: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa are potential biomarkers for diagnosing acute exacerbation in diseased lungs. Kuo et al. reveal that VOCs activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor to exacerbate airway mucus pathology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evidence of dengue transmission and a diverse Aedes mosquito virome on the Congo’s Angola border
item.description: Mosquito sequencing along the DRC-Angola border reveals diverse viruses and evidence of ongoing dengue transmission. This study shows that xenosurveillance has the potential to improve emerging infectious disease detection and prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adaptive oncogenesis of β-catenin emerges from declining liver tissue integrity
item.description: Despite being a common driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), oncogenic β-catenin is ineffective at initiating liver cancer on its own. Here the authors show that β-catenin mutations as a single genetic event confer negative fitness in the healthy liver, while driving clonal expansion and tumorigenesis as liver tissue integrity declines with chronic liver disease or aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clinical utility of molecular residual disease detection in early-stage resected EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: For patients with resected EGFR-mutated lung cancer, effective strategies to guide post-surgical surveillance remain an unmet need. Here, the author shows that a personalized blood test may indicate molecular residual disease months before radiological progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: MRICombo: a deep-learning-based framework for universal volumetric segmentation grading-staging and malignancy detection across heterogeneous MRI
item.description: Existing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) deep learning models are often task- or sequence-specific. Here, the authors present MRICombo, which segments anatomy, labels tumor types, and supports grading, staging and malignancy detection across heterogeneous sequences.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting m 6 A writer METTL3 with engineered nanovesicles reduces neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo
item.description: Strategies to modulate neuroinflammation have broad therapeutic potential. Here, the authors develop siMETTL3-hNVs, nanovesicles carrying siRNA targeting METTL3, and show they can reduce neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo.
